Encrypted DVDs can now be handled, and the switch that was supposed to do that in the meantime is fixed: it never worked.

## ✨ Added

- **`INSTALL_LIBDVDCSS=true` builds `libdvdcss` on the first start.** The library is not shipped in the image. The container downloads the release tarball from VideoLAN's own mirror, checks it against a checksum pinned inside the container, and compiles it on your machine. About 15 seconds on a first start, about a second afterwards from the cache under `/config/handbrake/libdvdcss/`. In Unraid it is a template variable under **Show more settings**, off by default. Whether decrypting a disc you own is lawful depends on where you live, which is why nothing happens unless you set it.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **The switch shipped on 1 September did nothing at all.** It used `libdvd-pkg`, which fetches its source from `code.videolan.org`. That host now answers with a bot-protection page instead of the archive, the checksum check fails, and the build never completes. Setting the variable installed 31 packages of build tooling and produced no library.
- **Every error path in that oneshot was dead code.** `if command | sed` reports the exit status of `sed`, so a failed `apt-get` or `dpkg` was read as success. The worst case was the cache: a broken cached package logged `done (cached)` on every single start and was never discarded.
- **A failed build no longer claims success.** Each step now says which one failed and why, and the container starts normally without the library either way.
- **`No Title Found` is documented properly.** `Scanning title 1 of 1` is the state every HandBrake scan starts in and does not mean the disc was read. Troubleshooting now names the one Activity-log line that tells the cases apart.

## 🧪 Testing

- CI now turns `INSTALL_LIBDVDCSS=true` on and insists on a loadable `libdvdcss.so.2`, on both architectures, on a cold build and from the cache. It also asserts that the image itself never ships the library. None of that path had ever run in CI before.
- Lint now diffs the shipped scripts against the Dockerfile's `chmod +x` list. A service missing from that list is refused by s6 with exit 126 and takes the WebUI down with it, which is exactly what happened during 1 September's work.

Reported in [#2](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/handbrake/issues/2), which stays open until a disc has actually been scanned on real hardware.
